metadata.title: TIMSS and PIRLS 2011 Relationships Report
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center, Boston College

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the TIMSS & PIRLS 2011 fourth-grade combined database containing only students assessed in reading, mathematics, and science. Analyses are estimated in Mplus with a two-level structure (students within countries; and country as the between-level in the pooled model), and the Mplus “Complex” option is used with school as the cluster variable to correct standard errors for the clustered sampling design. The authors explicitly state that individual student case weights (HOUWGT) are used in the analyses. Plausible values for the three achievement outcomes are handled via Mplus imputation across all five PVs, and parameter estimates/standard errors are combined across PVs; therefore, the weighting and PV procedures are integrated into the estimation rather than treated as post-hoc adjustments.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The chapter reports how plausible values (five PVs) are handled in Mplus, but it does not describe a specific missing-data strategy for questionnaire items or other covariates (e.g., listwise/pairwise deletion or multiple imputation). This is a reporting gap because missingness in background questionnaires is common in large-scale assessments, and the path model relies on multiple latent constructs built from questionnaire items. The authors’ focus is on PV-based estimation and model fit indices, leaving the missing-data handling for predictors/indicators unspecified.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the TIMSS & PIRLS 2011 fourth-grade combined international database containing only students assessed in all three subjects (reading, mathematics, and science) in the 34 participating countries plus 3 benchmarking entities (37 participants total). The chapter’s path-model estimation uses pooled data across all 37 participants and also fits separate saturated models for each country/benchmarking entity; for the country-by-country models, the text notes that Ireland has missing data on some variables.

data.outcome_summary: This chapter uses TIMSS 2011 mathematics and science and PIRLS 2011 reading at the fourth grade, leveraging a special combined database where the same students are assessed in all three domains. The analytic strategy is a multilevel path-model framework estimated in Mplus: a pooled “common model” treats countries as the between-level and students within countries as the within-level, and then separate saturated models are estimated for each of the 34 countries plus 3 benchmarking entities (37 participants). Achievement outcomes are handled with five plausible values per domain, and the authors report model fit using chi-square (with mean across PVs), RMSEA, CFI, and SRMR. The study uses individual student case weights (HOUWGT) and the Mplus “Complex” option with school as the cluster variable. Key results show that parental education is strongly associated with achievement through books, home literacy/numeracy activities, and early abilities, while gender differences are most consistent for reading via a stronger emphasis on literacy activities for girls; however, the chapter does not document missing-data handling for questionnaire indicators.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction corresponds to an IEA/OECD-style relationships report chapter that is not an ML predictive paper: it uses path modeling/latent-variable measurement and multilevel estimation rather than machine-learning algorithms. As a result, ML technique fields are intentionally empty and main_findings are not fabricated. The chapter is still empirical and reports standardized effects and mediation patterns, but these are not ML model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC) and therefore do not map to the StructuredFinding schema.
